background_notes.fact: For a finite complex basis (e_i) indexed by J, every w∈V has unique coefficients c_i with w=Σ_i c_i e_i. If h is complex-linear, h(e_i)=μ_i e_i and h(w)=νw, then (μ_i−ν)c_i=0 for each i.

background_notes.justification: Spanning gives an expression as a finite linear combination of the e_i. Independence makes two such expressions have identical coefficients by subtracting them. Apply linearity to the finite expansion, subtract ν times that expansion, and use independence to set every coefficient (μ_i−ν)c_i equal to zero. These are the ordinary basis properties used explicitly in S003.

background_notes.fact: For every natural r, r! is nonzero in ℂ, 0!=1 and (r+1)!=(r+1)r!. For r≥1, r/r!=1/(r−1)! in ℂ. A complex-linear operator commutes with multiplication by these inverse factorial scalars.

grounds.reason: D004 defines divided powers using the ordinary factorial and the complex scalar field.

background_notes.justification: Each positive integer is nonzero in the characteristic-zero field ℂ, so its finite factorial product is nonzero. Split off the last factor of the product and cancel it in the field; the r=0 product is one. Scalar compatibility follows from complex linearity. This justifies the cancellations in the displayed action calculations, including both endpoints.
